summary.text: Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates of the class Aves, set apart by feathers, toothless beaked jaws, hard-shelled eggs and a strong yet lightweight skeleton.
There are over 11,000 living species, ranging from the 5.5-centimetre bee hummingbird to the 2.8-metre common ostrich.
Birds evolved from earlier theropods, which makes them the only living dinosaurs, and their closest living relatives are the crocodilians.

facts.label: Biggest group
facts.value: More than half are passerines, or perching birds

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: Bee hummingbird at 5.5 centimetres, ostrich at 2.8 metres

items.prompt: A child at a museum asks whether any dinosaurs are still alive. What is the best answer?

options.label: No: only their crocodile cousins survive today
Yes: birds evolved from theropods and are living dinosaurs
Yes, but only birds that have lost flight count
No: they all died out when the pterosaurs did

items.explain: Birds evolved from earlier theropods and are the only extant members of Dinosauria; crocodilians are their closest living relatives, not dinosaurs themselves.

items.prompt: Penguins cannot fly, yet they have wings. What is the best explanation?

options.label: Penguin wings are a different organ that never came from forelimbs
Penguins are not true birds, so the rule about wings fails
Penguin wings are too small to count as proper wings
Wings gave birds flight, but later evolution led some groups to lose it

items.explain: Wings are modified forelimbs that gave birds the ability to fly, though further evolution has led to the loss of flight in some birds, including penguins.

items.prompt: If you pick one of the world's bird species at random, which kind is it most likely to be?

options.label: A perching bird
A flightless bird
A seabird
A swimming waterbird

items.explain: More than half of the world's bird species are passerine, or perching, birds.

items.prompt: Two birds of a typical species raise chicks together this season. How long is their partnership most likely to last?

options.label: For life, as in nearly all species
Only until the eggs are laid
Just this breeding season, perhaps a few more
Only until the chicks hatch

items.explain: Most bird species are socially monogamous, usually for one breeding season at a time, sometimes for years, and rarely for life.

items.prompt: A biologist says birds are reptiles. Under which kind of classification is that correct?

options.label: Modern cladistic classification
The traditional Linnaean system, with birds in their own class
Both systems, since birds lay hard-shelled eggs
Neither system, since birds are warm-blooded

items.explain: Traditional Linnaean taxonomy gave birds their own class, but in the modern cladistic sense of the term birds are considered reptiles.

items.prompt: Many birds cannot fly, but nearly all still have wings. Which known groups have none at all?

options.label: Penguins and other swimming birds
Ostriches and the other ratites
Island birds that lost flight
The extinct moa and elephant birds

items.explain: The only known groups without wings are the extinct moa and elephant birds; ratites and penguins still have wings.
